title: Concurrent Team Claim Prevention with Database Locking
i_want: To prevent multiple users from claiming the same team simultaneously using database-level locking mechanisms
so_that: Data integrity is maintained and exactly one user successfully claims each team, even under high concurrency

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Concurrent claim attempts with pessimistic locking
given: User A and User B submit claim requests within 50ms of each other
System uses SELECT FOR UPDATE (PostgreSQL) or row-level locking
when: Both requests attempt to acquire lock on team record
First request (User A) acquires lock successfully
Second request (User B) waits for lock or times out
then: User A's transaction commits successfully with team claimed
User B's request fails with HTTP 409 Conflict
Error message: 'Team was just claimed by another user. Please select a different team.'
Database maintains exactly one claim record
No orphaned or duplicate claims exist
Lock is released within 5 seconds maximum

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Optimistic locking with version-based conflict detection
given: Team record has version number field (e.g., version=1)
System uses optimistic locking for read-heavy operations
Two users load the same team data simultaneously
when: User A submits claim with version=1
User A's update succeeds, incrementing version to 2
User B submits claim with stale version=1
then: User B's request returns HTTP 409 Conflict
Error includes: 'This team was just claimed. Refresh to see current availability.'
Retry-After header suggests 1-second delay
Client auto-refreshes team list on conflict
Audit log records both attempts with timestamps
No data corruption occurs

given: Database uses SERIALIZABLE or REPEATABLE READ isolation
Multiple concurrent transactions accessing same team records
when: Transaction B reads same teams before A commits
Transaction A claims team and commits
Transaction B attempts to claim same team
then: Transaction B detects serialization failure
System retries Transaction B automatically (max 3 attempts)
If retry fails, return HTTP 409 with clear message
No dirty reads or phantom reads occur
ACID properties are maintained
Performance impact < 200ms for conflict resolution

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Distributed lock with Redis for horizontal scaling
when: Server A acquires Redis lock 'team:raiders:lock' with TTL=10s
Server B attempts same lock and fails
Server A processes claim and releases lock
Or lock expires after 10s if server crashes
then: Only one server processes claim at a time
Lock expires automatically to prevent deadlocks
Monitoring alerts on frequent lock timeouts
Lock acquisition time < 50ms in 99th percentile
Failed lock attempts return immediately with 409
Idempotency key prevents duplicate processing
All attempts logged with nanosecond timestamps
Log includes: user_id, team_id, attempt_time, lock_acquired, commit_status
Winner and losers clearly identified in logs
Metrics track: conflict rate, resolution time, retry success rate
Dashboards show concurrent claim patterns
Alerts trigger if conflict rate > 5% of claims

optimistic_locking.version_field: INTEGER version column on teams table
optimistic_locking.update_pattern: UPDATE teams SET claimed_by=?, version=version+1 WHERE id=? AND version=?

distributed_locking.ttl: 10 seconds with automatic extension for long operations
distributed_locking.quorum: Majority of Redis nodes for lock acquisition

idempotency.response_caching: Cache successful response for idempotent retry

conflict_response.message: This team was just claimed by another user. Please select a different team.

lock_timeout.message: Unable to process claim due to high demand. Please try again.

performance_requirements.throughput: Handle 1000 concurrent claim attempts per second

load_testing: Simulate 100 users claiming same team within 1-second window
Verify exactly 1 successful claim and 99 proper conflict responses
Test with 10,000 concurrent users across different teams
Measure lock contention and resolution times
chaos_testing: Kill application server mid-transaction to test lock expiry
Simulate network partitions in distributed lock scenario
Test database connection failures during claim processing
Verify recovery with zero data corruption
unit_tests: Mock concurrent transactions with race condition simulation
Test all lock timeout and retry paths
Verify idempotency key generation and validation
integration_tests: End-to-end concurrent claim test with real database
Redis distributed lock test with multiple app instances
